EL.thesis_one_line: Prestige beauty turnaround is real and accelerating, but the price already assumes more margin recovery than one clean year can prove.
kill_criteria: Organic net sales growth falls back below 3% for two consecutive quarters (it has ranged 3-5% for the last four quarters; a reversal would break the accelerating trend).
Adjusted operating margin fails to reach at least 12.0% for FY2027 (vs. the guided 12.7-13.5%).
Any new goodwill/intangible impairment or litigation settlement charge exceeding $100m is recorded in FY2027.

GAAP operating income is negative for two consecutive quarters in FY2027 (it was negative in Q4 FY2026 alone due to restructuring cash costs - a repeat pattern would suggest the restructuring is not on the disclosed timeline).
key_adverse_facts: FY2025 GAAP diluted EPS was $(3.15), driven by a $911m Americas goodwill impairment, a $375m Asia/Pacific intangible impairment, and $159m of Talcum-litigation settlement charges.

An $84m loss contingency (net of insurance recoveries) for a pending securities class-action settlement was recorded in FY2026 - the underlying allegations were not detailed in the sources reviewed this pass and should be read directly in the FY2026 10-K's legal-proceedings item before sizing any position.
Q4 FY2026 GAAP operating income was still negative ($(39)m) due to continued restructuring cash charges, even as the turnaround narrative strengthened.
Triage itself flagged the highest one-year volatility in its batch (49%) and noted the China/travel-retail recovery must prove durable beyond one quarter - genuine, not manufactured, uncertainty.
data_conflicts: Triage framed the 27x NTM P/E as 'reasonable against that growth'; this dossier's reverse DCF finds the 2026-09-25 price implies ~11.7% sustained 10-year FCF growth at a sourced-beta (1.274) WACC of ~9.8%, above this dossier's independent evidence-based base case of ~7-8% - the triage's optimism does not survive a formal reverse-DCF check, which is the basis for overturning triage's implicit 'advance' framing to WATCH.
EL.horizon: 12-36 months (if the WATCH condition is met)
EL.confidence_in_thesis: medium - the operating turnaround evidence (accelerating organic growth, FCF nearly doubled) is strong and consistent across four straight quarterly releases, but it is only one fiscal year old, sits alongside a real recent litigation/impairment history, and the reverse DCF shows the price is already ahead of a conservative base case

AMP.thesis_one_line: Capital-light wealth and asset manager growing assets under management double-digits, returning most earnings to shareholders, priced under 10 times earnings.
kill_criteria: TTM ROE falls below 40% (vs. ~62% now) for two consecutive quarters - would indicate faster-than-expected mean reversion.
Total AUM+AUA growth (YoY) falls below 5% for two consecutive quarters (vs. 13-19% segment growth now).
Capital returned to shareholders falls below 60% of operating earnings for two consecutive quarters (vs. ~91% in Q2 2026) - would signal a capital-return policy change.
Any named, material litigation or regulatory enforcement matter (e.g. a cash-sweep-program-style industry action) is disclosed in a future 10-Q's Legal Proceedings item.
Adjusted operating EPS YoY growth turns negative for any quarter (it has been +16% to +22% in each of the last four).
Advice & Wealth Management total client net flows negative for two consecutive quarters (+$3.1bn in Q2 2026). Added by RA10 2026-10-06.
Ameriprise Financial long-term debt to capital above 40% (37.5% at 30 Jun 2026, includes $750m prefunding). Added by RA10 2026-10-06.
key_adverse_facts: ROE (62% TTM) sits at roughly the 80th percentile of AMP's own 10-year history per V1's own dataset - a real, sourced mean-reversion risk, not a remote one.

GAAP diluted EPS is materially more volatile quarter to quarter than Adjusted operating EPS (e.g. $5.00 to $10.57 in consecutive quarters) due to insurance/annuity mark-to-market effects in the legacy Retirement & Protection Solutions block.

Net debt was wrong in the original: Ameriprise Financial long-term debt is $3,823m (up from $3,079m after $750m of senior notes on 9 Jun 2026, accession 0001104659-26-071727), debt-to-capital 37.5% vs 33.6%; the -$6.0bn 'net cash' is Yahoo's consolidated figure, mostly regulated-subsidiary cash. Corrected by RA10 2026-10-06.

Growth is market-driven: Q2 2026 AWM total client net flows were $3.1bn (-28% YoY) and Asset Management AUM net flows -$6.5bn, so 13-19% AUM growth is mostly market appreciation. Two senior executives retired in 2026 (8-Ks 12 Feb and 20 May).
data_conflicts: V1's bull-case scenario (+67.7%/yr annualised, 3yr) compounds an 80th-percentile ROE assumption with 8.3%/yr assumed share-count shrinkage for three straight years; this dossier flags the resulting >3x price outcome as a likely modeling artefact of compounding two aggressive assumptions together rather than a plausible upper bound - this does not change V1's verdict or base case, only flags the bull case specifically as overstated. [RA10: V1 bull case retired; V1 base-case ROE reversion to 30% also not supportable.]
AMP.confidence_in_thesis: medium-high - multi-quarter primary-source evidence of AUM and adjusted-EPS growth, clean red-flag scan; capped because the corrected P/B test leaves no margin, flows are weak and parent debt/capital is rising (RA10 2026-10-06)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: This dossier's primary-source read agrees with V1's 'fair' verdict and treats V1's base case (implied ROE mean-reverting toward the 50th percentile of AMP's own 10-year history, ~30% ROE) as the operative base case here. One reservation flagged (not a disagreement with the verdict): V1's bull-case compounding looks overstated (see data_conflicts). RA10 2026-10-06: restated on a corrected basis. COE 10.6% (5.17% + 1.13 x 4.8%) puts the implied ROE at 55.0% on total equity (46.3% ex-AOCI) against an adjusted operating ROE ex-AOCI of 55.0% and a 50% base: in line, no margin of safety. V1 base ROE reversion to 30% is not supportable (equity was $8-9bn in 2012-2014 against $6.4bn now); V1 bull case retired.
